The files in this folder are data of the Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD),
from its open-data server, https://opendata.dwd.de. DWD's legal notice,
https://www.dwd.de/DE/service/rechtliche_hinweise/rechtliche_hinweise_node.html,
read on 2026-11-21, says of them: "Alle frei zugänglichen Geodaten und
Geodatendienste sowie die als hochwertige Datensätze / high value datasets
(HVD) festgelegten Leistungen des DWD dürfen unter den Bedingungen der
Lizenz Creative Commons BY 4.0 (CC BY 4.0) unter Beigabe eines
Quellenvermerks weiterverwendet werden."
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/. Quelle: Deutscher
Wetterdienst. They are not covered by the licence of the code around them.

They were recorded on 2026-11-21 from
https://opendata.dwd.de/weather/radar/radolan/ry/, without a key, with
curl. Each is the whole answer to one request of the adapter, unchanged:

    list.html   GET /weather/radar/radolan/ry/
                asked at 11:43:45 UTC, 85,577 bytes: the server's list of
                the folder, 576 frames from 2026-11-19 11:45 to 2026-11-21
                11:40 UTC, and the newest once more under the name
                "latest"

    raa01-ry_10000-2611211135-dwd---bin.hdf5   56,477 bytes
    raa01-ry_10000-2611211140-dwd---bin.hdf5   57,348 bytes
                GET /weather/radar/radolan/ry/<name>
                asked at 11:55 UTC: the two frames the list names last,
                the rain of 11:30 to 11:35 and of 11:35 to 11:40 UTC. The
                server dated them 11:35:17 and 11:40:17 UTC
                (Last-Modified): a frame is there some twenty seconds
                after the five minutes it is of.

A frame is one picture of the composite RY of DWD's RADOLAN routine: 1100
by 1200 pixels of one kilometre, a rain rate in each or the mark that no
radar saw the place. On that morning it rained lightly over the south of
Bavaria and the north of Tirol, which is why these two were taken: the
first region's box holds some 6,500 cells of rain in each. A frame names
DWD's address for the product (radolan@dwd.de) in its attributes; it holds
nothing about any person.

The list names 576 frames and this folder holds two. A run over the
recorded answers is therefore told that the frames up to 11:30 UTC are
held already (fixtures::held_until), and asks for the two after it.

The folder damaged/ holds what is NOT DWD's data as published:

    damaged/cut_after_4096_bytes.hdf5   the first 4096 bytes of the frame
                                        of 11:35, to test a file that is
                                        cut short
    damaged/not_a_frame.html            written by hand: the page a web
                                        server sends for a file it does not
                                        have, to test an answer that is no
                                        frame

Other damage is done to a recorded frame in memory by the tests that need
it (another product's name, another projection, data that unpacks to more
than the picture holds); each test says what it changes.

Looked at on the same day and not kept here: the frame the server had as
"latest" at 11:45:25 UTC (the one of 11:45, 57,432 bytes), and the frame of
2026-11-19 12:35 UTC (434,915 bytes), from a morning of rain over most of
Germany, to measure how large a frame of the first region is when it rains
widely (docs/data-sources.md has the figures).

To record them again: fetch the list, then the two frames it names last,
within the same five minutes; replace the three files; set the moments in
src/fixtures.rs (recorded_at, held_until, frames) and the names there; run
the tests with VENTI_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 and review what changed. The counts
the tests pin (cells of rain, pixels nobody saw) are of that moment and
will differ; a dry morning makes a poor recording. The server's
development mode serves these frames, and its golden files change with
them.

A frame is what radars measured from afar. It is no statement that a place
is dry, or that it can be flown.
